FACT_ID: sec09-R01 | anchor: A03
Parking distances differ by object: 15 feet from a hydrant, 20 feet from a fire station driveway on your side, 30 feet from a stop sign or signal, and 50 feet from the nearest rail. [A03]
Why it matters: group no-parking distances; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec09-F34, sec09-F35, sec09-F36, sec09-F39 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-R02 | anchor: A03
A fire station driveway needs 20 feet of clearance on the same side of the street but 75 feet on the opposite side when that distance is marked. [A03]
Why it matters: group no-parking distances; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec09-F35 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-R03 | anchor: A04
Parking near a crosswalk requires 20 feet, but near an intersection without a crosswalk the gap is 15 feet. [A04]
Why it matters: group no-parking distances; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec09-F42 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec09-R04 | anchor: A02
Wheels turn toward the curb when parked downhill and away from the curb when parked uphill. [A02]
Why it matters: group hill parking; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec09-F20 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-R05 | anchor: A02
When parallel parking, pull up 2 to 5 feet beside the car ahead, and finish no more than 6 to 12 inches from the curb. [A02]
Why it matters: group parallel parking; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec09-F22, sec09-F25 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-R06 | anchor: A01
If stuck on tracks with a train coming or gates down, get out and call 911; if no train is in sight and nothing is activated, get everyone out and call the railroad emergency number on the blue sign. [A01]
Why it matters: group stuck on tracks; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec09-F12, sec09-F13 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-R07 | anchor: A01
Passive crossings use signs and markings only, while active crossings add gates, flashing lights or bells that announce a train. [A01]
Why it matters: group crossing types; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec09-F03, sec09-F05 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-R08 | anchor: A01
You must clear the far side of the tracks by 6 feet before crossing into backed-up traffic, and you get only about 20 seconds of warning once the signals start. [A01]
Why it matters: group crossing safety; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec09-F10, sec09-F11 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-R09 | anchor: A03
A disability plate or placard lets you use a disability space, but only a placard with the yellow sticker gives free parking. [A03]
Why it matters: group disability parking; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec09-F27, sec09-F28 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-R10 | anchor: A03
A parking ticket goes to the vehicle's owner, or to the person leasing it if the vehicle is leased, not simply to whoever parked it. [A03]
Why it matters: group parking violations; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec09-F32 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0052]
